product.title: AI inside your product
product.text: When it genuinely helps your users, I build AI right into your site or app.
items: An assistant that answers from your own content
A back office that helps write and sort

om.name: A whole club’s digital ecosystem
om.need: Nine months rebuilding om.fr as part of the club’s rebrand: 30+ pages, a design system shared by four teams, headless Sanity and an API-first architecture built to absorb match-night traffic spikes.
done: Match Day block, match page and Live Match to follow every game as it happens
Memberships and upsell mechanics towards higher tiers
Fixtures, results and league table fed by sports data
Content driven from Sanity, with every block mapped to the CMS

ami.name: AMI du quartier
ami.need: Ami Paris celebrates friendship in the neighborhoods it loves. Everyone shares their story (flowers on a Sunday, coffee at the same spot), pinned on a map and browsed like a roll of film rather than a feed.
done: Two-level interactive map: neighborhood zones first, then individual places on zoom
Private addresses anonymized and grouped by street, points of interest pinned individually
Filters by type of moment, managed from the back office
Feed that alternates personal, community, AMI-curated and brand content depending on the user’s profile

fcl.name: A hundred years of Merlus
fcl.need: FC Lorient was turning 100. Not just another anniversary site: a tribute to the fans, giving promotions, cup nights and names still quoted twenty years later the weight they carry in their memory.
done: All the development work: pages, dynamic elements and CSS integration
Custom-built animations, micro-interactions and transitions
Headless WordPress: legends, kits, matches, goals, seasons and photos modeled as schemas
Cache-invalidation webhooks: every publish goes live immediately

pgw.name: France’s biggest gaming show
pgw.need: The event’s digital storefront: spark interest, inform fast and drive ticket sales, on desktop and mobile alike, while holding up under traffic spikes from announcements and ticket launches.
done: Pages and dynamic elements, CSS integration
Animations and micro-interactions true to the gaming world
Headless Sanity: content mapped to the CMS so the team can work on its own
Cache-invalidation webhooks on every publish

foncia.name: Real-estate transaction ERP
foncia.need: The central tool for Foncia group’s transaction teams, supporting the whole sale and purchase cycle of a property, from first contact to signature.
done: React interfaces and reusable components, built to stay maintainable at scale
Node.js services in a microservices architecture, run and orchestrated with Docker
GitLab CI pipelines and review apps to validate each change in isolation before merge
Functional and technical acceptance testing (UAT) before every release
Internal packages published to a private npm registry (Verdaccio)

About.label: (05) About
About.bio: I started out as a mechanical engineer and became a full stack developer because I love building useful things. That path taught me to listen, understand the need, ask the right questions, then deliver a clean product. Based in Paris, my goal comes down to choosing the right tools, testing, and shipping a product where I own every detail.
